Ofcom's social tariffs guidance was published on 6 March 2024.
Ofcom's social tariffs guidance was last updated on 22 June 2026.
Social tariffs are lower-cost broadband and phone packages for people claiming Universal Credit, Pension Credit and some other benefits.
Ofcom stated that current social-tariff prices ranged from £10 to £24.
Ofcom stated that most listed social tariffs offered speeds over 30 Mbit/s.
If a social tariff has setup costs, Ofcom said they should only be small and disclosed before signup.
A customer whose provider offers a social tariff can switch to it at any time free of charge.
Ofcom stated that the price of a social tariff will not rise mid-contract.
Ofcom stated that customers do not pay a fee to leave a social tariff before contract end.
If the customer or someone in the household claims Universal Credit, Ofcom said they could switch to any listed tariff.
Ofcom stated that all major providers also include Pension Credit, Employment and Support Allowance, Jobseeker's Allowance and Income Support.
Some providers may include additional benefits such as Personal Independence Payment and Attendance Allowance.
The person receiving the qualifying benefit needs to be the main person on the contract.
Ofcom cautioned that providers might not cover all premises in the regions listed.
Wildanet's listed tariff was available only to Universal Credit recipients at the page update date.
Ofcom's bill-saving research was published on 26 February 2026 and last updated on 30 June 2026.
Average advertised broadband prices across speed categories fell by 6% in real terms in the preceding year.
SIM-only plans accounted for half of pay-monthly subscriptions, up from 44% a year earlier.
Average prices for unlimited-data SIM-only plans fell by 8% in real terms.
Ofcom estimated that 28% of broadband customers were out of contract.
In-contract broadband customers spent £7 to £9 less per month on average than out-of-contract customers.
Eighteen percent of households switched internet provider in the latest year, up from 14% in 2023.
Ofcom stated that One Touch Switch had been used by more than two million customers.
Ofcom stated that around eight in ten UK homes had access to full-fibre broadband.
Budget mobile brands had consistently offered deals 40% to 50% cheaper than average prices over recent years.
Seventy percent of households buying broadband and landline together made no outgoing landline call in the latest year.
Twenty-nine percent of pay-monthly mobile users consumed 2 GB of data or less per month.
Ofcom's Communications Affordability Tracker page was last updated on 14 May 2026.
The tracker covers affordability experiences for home broadband, mobile phone, landline and pay-TV services.
Ofcom published its money-saving tips page on 1 July 2026.
Ofcom said new communications contracts are typically 12, 18 or 24 months long.
Ofcom said its affordability tracker is published biannually and includes awareness of social tariffs.
